steps.user_message: I need to prepare internal financial materials. Our company Northgate Consulting has $980K cash, 7 months runway, burn rate $85K/month, and revenue last quarter $1.1M. Can you help me with revenue growth and retention metrics? I need to get the finance narrative right.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with finance-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Thanks — I can help. First, one quick inconsistency to clarify so I give accurate numbers and the right narrative:

- You said Northgate has $980K cash, 7 months runway, and $85K/month burn. Cash ÷ burn = 980 / 85 ≈ 11.5 months, not 7 months. Is the 7-month runway number calculated after including other commitments (debt service, payroll commitments, taxes, one‑time payments), or is your reported burn rate the “operating burn” while the runway figure uses a larger “true” burn? Also:
  - Is the $1.1M “revenue last quarter” recurring (MRR/ARR-style) or mostly one-time/project revenue?
  - Do you have prior-quarter revenue, customer counts, MRR/ARR, churn (logo or dollar), and expansion revenue data? With those I can compute exact growth and retention metrics.

Below I’ll list the most useful metrics, formulas, example calculations you can run quickly, suggested targets, and a short finance narrative you can adapt for internal materials. If you give me the additional numbers I’ll compute the exact values and write slide-ready copy.

Key metrics to prepare (what to show and why)
- Quarterly Revenue Growth (QoQ)
  - Formula: (This quarter rev − Prior quarter rev) / Prior quarter rev
  - Need prior quarter revenue. Example: if prior quarter = $1.0M, QoQ = (1.1 − 1.0) / 1.0 = 10%
- Year-over-Year Growth (YoY)
  - Formula: (This quarter rev − Same quarter last year) / Same quarter last year
  - Use if you have prior-year quarter.
- ARR / Run-rate
  - If revenue is recurring, ARR = MRR × 12 or last 12 months recurring revenue (LTM).
  - Example: $1.1M last quarter → monthly average ≈ $366.7K → annualized run-rate ≈ $1.47M.
- Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) — measures revenue lost from churn (no expansion)
  - Formula (quarterly): (Starting ARR from cohort − Churned revenue) / Starting ARR
  - Target: >90% for most SaaS; higher is better for enterprise.
- Net Revenue Retention (NRR) — includes expansion/contraction
  - Formula: (Starting ARR + Expansion − Contraction − Churn) / Starting ARR
  - Target: >100% is ideal (means existing customers are net-growing).
- Logo (customer) churn and Dollar churn
  - Logo churn = (#customers lost over period) / (#customers at period start)
  - Dollar churn = (revenue lost from churn) / (revenue at period start)
  - Monthly churn target depends on model (SaaS <1–2% monthly is good).
- ARPA / ARPU (Average revenue per account)
  - Formula: Total recurring revenue / #active customers
- LTV and CAC payback (if you track CAC)
  - LTV = ARPA × Gross Margin / churn rate (approx.)
  - CAC payback = CAC / monthly gross margin contribution
- Cash runway / breakeven math (cash and burn clarity)
  - Simple runway = Cash / Net burn per month
  - If you want to reach breakeven, compute revenue required to cover current burn:
    - If fixed monthly burn is $85K and gross margin on revenue is m, required recurring revenue contribution = burn / m (if you need revenue to cover burn). But you must be careful: if current top-line already exceeds burn, net burn might be negative — need cash-flow view (collections, one-time vs recurring).

Immediate checks you should run (I can compute if you provide the numbers)
1. Confirm whether the $1.1M is recurring or one-off revenues and provide prior quarter(s).
2. Provide:
   - Prior quarter revenue (and same quarter last year if available)
   - #customers at start/end of quarter, new logos, churned logos
   - Expansion revenue (upsells) and contraction revenue
   - MRR or ARR if available
   - Any deferred revenue / customer prepayments (cash vs GAAP difference)
3. Confirm whether the $85K burn is gross burn or net of operating revenue.

Example calculations (with assumptions) to illustrate the narrative
- Revenue run-rate from last quarter: 1.1M / 3 = $366.7K/month → annualized ≈ $4.4M (if you meant $1.1M/month? clarify). If $1.1M is the whole quarter, annualized run-rate = $1.1M × 4 = $4.4M.
- If quarterly revenue = $1.1M and prior quarter = $1.0M → QoQ = 10% (good positive growth).
- If ARR (annualized) is $4.4M and monthly burn is $85K, then monthly revenue (recurring) ≈ $366.7K, which more than covers burn (net cash positive from operations) — explain why your runway number might differ (cash timing, one-time expenses, capex, or commitments).

Suggested finance narrative (short, slide-ready)
- Opening summary: “Last quarter we recorded $1.1M in revenue (quarterly). We have $980K cash on hand and report an operating burn of $85K/month. We are currently projecting X–Y months of runway (see note on calculation).”
- Growth story: “Quarter-over-quarter revenue increased by [X%], driven by [new logos / price adjustments / upsell]. Our run-rate (annualized) is $[ARR].”
- Retention story (if data available): “Our Net Revenue Retention is [NRR%], reflecting successful upsells/expansion and a logo churn of [logo churn%]. Gross Revenue Retention sits at [GRR%], indicating we retain [X%] of base revenue absent expansion.”
- Cash/risk posture: “With current cash and burn, we have [7/11.5] months of runway. Primary near-term risks are [high churn, large one-time client concentration, slow AR collections].”
- Action plan / ask:
  - Short term (0–3 months): reduce discretionary spend by $X/month, tighten collections, prioritize renewal/expansion opportunities that increase NRR.
  - Medium term (3–9 months): target NRR >100% via upsells and pricing changes, aim to reduce churn by X points.
  - Fundraising / options: if runway is <9 months, prepare a bridge or raise; if runway >9–12 months, prioritize margin improvement and organic growth.

KPIs and visuals to include in slides
- Top line: Quarterly revenue (last 4 quarters) chart — show QoQ%
- ARR / run-rate trend (12-month run-rate)
- NRR and GRR with target lines (e.g., 100%/90%)
- Churn (monthly and quarterly) and ARPA trend
- Cash runway chart (cash balance vs months at current burn) with “plan” scenarios (reduce burn, grow revenue +10%/20%)
- Waterfall showing how churn, contraction, and expansion impact revenue from one quarter to the next

Recommended targets (benchmarks)
- NRR >100% (excellent), 100% acceptable
- GRR >90%
- Monthly churn <1–2% (SaaS benchmark; adjust by business model)
- CAC payback <12 months (if you acquire customers at a cost)
- Maintain minimum runway of 9–12 months while fundraising or 6+ months if no raise planned — pick the target consistent with your hiring/commitment plans.

Next steps I can do for you
- If you give prior-quarter revenue and churn/expansion numbers I’ll calculate QoQ growth, GRR, NRR, churn, ARR, and produce a concise one-page finance narrative and 3–4 slide bullet points.
- If you prefer, tell me which numbers you already have (prior quarter revenue, MRR/ARR, customer counts, expansion revenue, churn) and I’ll run the metrics and create the narrative text and KPI slide bullets.

Which data can you share now so I can compute the exact metrics and draft the narrative?
